attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Present-tense observation with an upper bound of 'a few months'. Splitting off the open-ended 'flip back and forth' forecast is right.

contract.note: Reading 'a few months' as about 3-4 months is an ordinary reading. The result depends on which capability index is used, and Marcus named none.

evidence.note: Epoch says no Chinese model had passed o3 (April 2025) by January 2026. That implies a gap of about 8 months, though the figure is inferred and Epoch did not state it for December.
In November 2025 Kimi K2 Thinking ranked behind only GPT-5 on this index, a gap of about 3 months. The month figure is inferred from the ranking.
OpenAI's own page dates the GPT-5 release, which is needed to turn e2's ranking into months.
Kimi was below even Opus 4 (May 2025) on agentic cyber and coding tasks, a gap of roughly 6 months or more there. It was ahead of GPT-5 on some math tests, so this cuts both ways.
Hassabis's 'maybe' a matter of months is hedged and vague. It does not show the gap was at most a few months.

reviews.rationale: The answer depends on the measure. On Artificial Analysis's index the gap was about 3 months, and Kimi led GPT-5 on some NIST math tests, which fits 'at most a few months'. On Epoch's index the gap was about 8 months, and on NIST's agentic tasks it was about 6 months or more, which exceeds it. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met across the main measures.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, replying to a Trump quote he cites in the post.

semantics.note: 'Not winning by a lot' becomes 'not far ahead'. That is faithful, and the present tense is kept.

contract.note: Measuring by model capability is fair: the surrounding text is about models and a lag of 'a few months'. Treating months as 'not a lot' and a year or more as 'a lot' is an ordinary plain reading.

evidence.note: Epoch: Chinese models trailed by months (7 on average, 4 to 14 since 2023), not years, even though the US held every frontier position.
A credible expert view from January 2026: Hassabis put the gap at a matter of months (hedged), and the article quotes Huang saying the US is 'not far ahead'.
The small Arena gap is measured in March 2026, a later period, so it is context only.
Private investment is a different metric from the contract's main measure of model capability, so it is context and does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Measured by model capability, evidence from around December 2025 puts the US lead at months, not years: Epoch shows roughly 7-8 months, and expert estimates say months. That meets the support condition. The large US lead in private investment is a different metric that the contract treats as secondary.
